content.text: {"receipt_id": "0c89fc849b5675b7ac41d96bb891ff3d33160c9078fbeaa8d170aec1d2c34d17", "evidence_id": "task", "source_sha256": "a655b6b0061b1d464b60257ef14b71e773b45e463f5c1a70f0e60f49a8657a82", "media_type": "text/plain", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 1, "content": "1: Propose one feasible CPU-only study of estimating a fixed regression coefficient from unlabeled covariate-shifted inputs. Frozen linear predictor y=w^Tz+b. Background says nuisance variation orthogonal to w can change without changing predictions, and blindly matching every latent dimension may move prediction-relevant moments. Return a concrete idea and core testable hypotheses; no experiments required. CPU budget 2 cores, 1 GiB, 10 minutes on synthetic linear data."}

{"receipt_id": "92019a8264ffff4b6207a90778f49b4a72ab9fb84075a385f94ad404d5a522f4", "evidence_id": "submission", "source_sha256": "60ea22e6325093dd41eb5e8e2ad952a01743021ee0031abfee412881c2ee3a56", "media_type": "text/plain", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 1, "content": "1: Use a frozen w. Project z into span(w) and its orthogonal complement. Match only the orthogonal component first; do not change its w projection, so predictions are unchanged. Treat this as a diagnostic/control, not an accuracy-improving method. Contrast with all-coordinate matching in environments where target change is confined to the orthogonal subspace versus where the predictive projection shifts. The contribution is an exact invariance sanity test and empirical diagnosis of when broad alignment is harmful, not a new adaptation algorithm. H1: orthogonal-only centering leaves predictions identical up to numeric error under either shift type; nonzero prediction change falsifies faithful implementation. H2: under purely orthogonal nuisance shift, all-coordinate matching offers no necessary predictive benefit and may introduce error from finite-sample predictive-moment estimation; no-adaptation and orthogonal-only are controls. H3: under predictive-direction shift, invariance alone cannot correct errors; label-shift/covariate-shift ambiguity prevents universal correction. Use independent synthetic test labels only for evaluation. Risks: test concerns a fixed linear head and synthetic shifts, not arbitrary nonlinear learned representations."}

{"receipt_id": "7623e3956873e797b3788cda21434919612f3f8f764ed2728cf97058e3ebb1d4", "evidence_id": "reference", "source_sha256": "b1bfa5024b020b55a40310ab0350b554f1191b01c88ab26edcd71dc4d8f625e2", "media_type": "text/plain", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 1, "content": "1: Prior A: align all coordinate means/variances. Prior B: do no adaptation. Known risk: unlabeled source-target differences may reflect label shift, not nuisance. Global novelty is not established. No access to target labels in adaptation, but separate synthetic held-out labels are available for evaluation."}
